title: os.Root
short_description: A directory handle that refuses to open anything outside itself, symlinks included.
summary: Path traversal has always been the application's problem in Go. You took a user-supplied name, joined it to a base directory, and hoped your validation was airtight. `os.Root` moves the check into the kernel-facing layer: every operation is resolved relative to an open directory, and anything that would escape it fails with `path escapes from parent`, even when the escape hatch is a symlink.
diagram_caption: Every path is resolved step by step against the open directory. The moment a component would leave it, the operation fails.
